notes.title: DevBlog: Feudal Activities
notes.content:
The life of Margrave of Amberspiel is full of concerns and worries. You have to balance between the interests of your vassals, resolve crises and at the same time remain an exemplary ruler worthy of the Sovereign's trust. That's quite a feat!

But even busy feudal lords sometimes get an evening of leisure. Do you want to breathe a sigh of relief and press “End of Turn”? Do not rush, because soon you will have many opportunities to spend the time with benefits… or at least to have fun.

Now we are actively developing core gameplay and we are pleased to introduce the Activities. This mechanic gives you more control over gameplay, more customization options, and lets you play your character the way you want.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36617318/2c2004dc2e33457d9674e7959f4e7b8b20b402ee.png[/img]

Work on this mechanic started with the thought that our Margrave, like a prospector in an adit, is constantly working: resolving disputes, executing and pardoning, organizing city building and dealing with plenty of other state issues.

Such a gameplay had two significant issues: firstly, the player mainly reacted to external events such as crises, conflicts, demands, always taking the role of the responder. In addition, as our testers noticed, suffered the immersion - it felt not like the life of the feudal lord in its entirety, but rather like an unceasing job. Truly, where have you seen a feudal lord who does nothing but works? That's how we arrived at the idea of giving the players control over what Konrad does in his spare time.

First of all, we asked: what, in principle, can a feudal lord do at his leisure? We thought, read and googled and an approximate list appeared (It is typical that the first one there is the activity “get drunk”).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36617318/1610976f66e8543271edbadb48cf83889bca5189.png[/img]
[i]The list looked like this.[/i]

This list was to be reworked into mechanics. At the very least, all this splendor had to be categorized. After all, we won't force the player to choose from a few dozen options every time. We tried different options. For example, we divided the areas of activity into economy, war and religion, into duty and leisure, into regular and unique activities.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36617318/45c23f380fa39cd3a9339403b52b0f334e05afe6.png[/img]

Ultimately, we decided to divide the activities according to their gameplay functions or, in other words, according to the game parameters that each group affects. The end result is this system:

[list]
[*] [b]Faction-related activities[/b]: temple visits, entertainment, and walks around the city will change your relationship with the Church, the Holders, or the Trade League, respectively. Most of the time the change will even be positive! Moreover, it could affect both a faction as a whole and its specific representatives.
[*] [b]Resource-related activities[/b]: such as conducting an audit and holding the trial will test your worth as a ruler and give you a good chance to earn gold or raise authority.
[*] [b]Activities related with Margrave himself[/b]: reading books from his father's library, self-improvement and… sleep. These activities do not seem like the others, and for a good reason. We'll tell more about them soon!
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36617318/79866e4ef484d67ee15f9dd7239a5425d86c83f0.png[/img]
[i]The Margrave's leisure will begin with a window like this[/i]

But how does all of that translate into gameplay? In quiet moments, the game will give you a “Free Evening”, opening a separate menu where you can choose something to your liking. The chosen activity will not only give you a direct and known effect (for example, visiting a temple will have a positive effect on the loyalty of the clergy), but will also let you play a small, two or three stages long, thematic event with unforeseen meetings, incidents and dilemmas. You will run into your old acquaintances or ordinary subjects as you walk the streets; discover unexpected items of expenditure during audits; be forced to choose between utility and justice during a trial.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36617318/3dd98edf29ee5a435516ee91e3d1157e43a24604.png[/img]

During any event, even recreational, you should follow common sense and knowledge from the game's Codex. Unfortunate decisions could inflict heavy losses. After all, the world of Demesne seems calm and blissful only at first glance. In fact, it is harsh and does not forgive mistakes. We hope you will appreciate this combination of story-based roleplaying and “numerical” game mechanics.

That's not the end of Margrave Konrad's leisure, because the next dev diary will be devoted to the mechanics of Ambition. Unlike Activities, Ambitions require constant time investment (maybe you'll even have to miss a couple of feasts!), but in return, provide long-term benefits that change the characteristics of your character and domain.

Stay with us!

And make sure to add Sovereign's Will to your Steam wishlist if you haven't already for some reason!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1047560/Sovereigns_Will/

notes.title: Demo Updated!
notes.content:
Hello to all of you who are waiting and hoping!

We're happy to announce that we're still alive and continuing to make the game despite all the hardships of indie development.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36617318/7b6f229470db149a6d0b7fbf234e9a541e5a3db1.png[/img]

In parallel with the development of the main version of the game we decided to update the demo as well. We would like to report on the latest changes.

[list]
[*] We completely rethought the first exposition events. Now you can learn more about the politics and religion of the game world from a special event, neatly woven into the overall story. However, if you want to go straight into the main events and gameplay, this particular event can be skipped freely. We'll be disappointed, but we understand.
[*] The Codex has been updated with new articles on the political structure, history and religion of the Demesne — right down to the commandments and architectural features of the temples. Yes, we're really getting into it.
[*] We developed an innovative system that allows you to freeze the state of the game world at any chosen point in time to randomly reproduce it at the player's command. Simply put, we now have a save and load.
[*] A lot of small interface fixes: colors, borders, interposition of elements. The Fallen One is in the details.
[*] Made a few improvements under the hood, which will allow more efficient creation of localizations (including fanmade).
[*] Created pages on [url=https://www.facebook.com/literalteam]Facebook[/url], [url=https://twitter.com/literal_team]Twitter[/url] and [url=https://vk.com/literalteam]VKontakte[/url]. They can now be accessed via social links in the main menu.
[*] Other little things that we ourselves have already forgotten.
[/list]
Thank you very much for your support!

notes.title: DevBlog: February plans
notes.content:
Hello!

We would like to make the development process more transparent, that's why we will try to regularly tell you what we are doing. 

In [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/1047560/announcements/detail/2949260380221271841]New Year post[/url] we said, that we would participate in Steam Game Festival in February. After closely examining our abilities, pros and cons we decided to skip February and take part in Summer Festival. Steam's rules forbid to take part in more than one Festival per year, so we decided to take more time to prepare. It won't affect our update schedule: demo will be updated on time.

And here are our plans on February:

1. [b]Codex[/b] overhaul: new articles on politics, history and religion. It is unnecessary to read them all, but if you want to know more about the world of the game, you'll definitely need them.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36617318/126f1f144f6b39ad27bcf0bc7db9cb36af30073f.jpg[/img]

2. [b]Mechanic of character visits[/b]: margrave doesn't have much time to deal with the conspiracy, so you will have to choose people to turn to for help. Powerful merchant, wise keeper of the archives, furious mercenary - everyone of them is your potential ally, but they all want something in return. Every time you hit the road you may gain the upper hand over the conspirators, but also you may lose everything with every wrong move.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36617318/77d3f76e3d213eeefc72b300ed3c447ac23a07aa.jpg[/img]

In the end the friends you choose will define your ability to cope with the plot and will shape your reign.  This is a new part of the story and it all will be available in demo!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36617318/21d3797e8d46ef6e15cd1aa2cdd7c8e3c809bc48.jpg[/img]

3. [b]Save&Load system[/b]: due to new additions to the available storyline these functions are vital. How do you think, should the player be given an opportunity to load the game after bad decisions? Share your thoughts in the comments!

4: [b]New random events[/b]: about conflicts of peasants and landlords, day-to-day life of native peoples and margrave's personal life. Your reign will become more diversified.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36617318/1b6eda21fcccc4af110887aa8975459c691bad20.jpg[/img]

5. And, of course, we will continue polishing and improving the UI, bug fixing and balancing. Please, continue sending us your ideas and reports! We read closely every one of them and take them into consideration when thinking of what to do next.

notes.title: Sovereign's Will: DevBlog #1
notes.content:
Hello! This is our first post about features and design process of Sovereign’s Will. We shall endeavour to post biweekly in the future.

[img]https://media.giphy.com/media/Pjy9KgSBT5EhZvvsX4/giphy.gif[/img]

In short, Sovereign’s Will is a turn-based strategy game, in which the player takes the role of medieval lord to participate in political intrigues, manage his lands and make choices that would influence both his own fate and fate of the realm. Game takes place in a massive empire that engulfs whole of known world and is ruled by the immortal Sovereign.

Right now we’re going to cover essential game elements, and in following posts we’re going to look at them more closely.

[h3]Political intrigues[/h3]
Protagonist is a young monarch, who has returned to his lands after long education in the distant capital and immediately got involved in the world of politics and court intrigues.

You’ll need to find approaches to [b]powerful people[/b]: feudals, church officials, merchants, who may become both loyal allies and dangerous enemies. Each of them has goals and character traits which must be taken into account for one to not become a victim of intrigues - political struggles often are no less cruel than open battles.

These men and women aren’t unified, though: they’re organised into [b]factions[/b], which struggle among themselves for power and wealth. You can use bribes, persuasion, spies and lobby for beneficial decisions to undermine some factions and to empower the others; However, you can crush all of them and establish uncontested rule of your own, if you fancy such an outcome - it isn’t easy, but very much possible.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36617318/71628c0c4261024a66fa3514826169a7cd547a9c.jpg[/img]

[h3]Decisions and consequences[/h3]
Life abounds in your lands: in a remote village peasants got accustomed to blood sacrifices, two nobles are unable to divide contested lands, and citizens are rebelling against increased taxes. You are a ruler of these lands, therefore they’re going to come to you with all their grievances, pleas and demands. You shouldn't forget about private matters either: your old friend from university asks you to accompany him on a pub crawl “just like old times”, a rich magnate asks for the hand of your sister, servants need supervision as well…

You have to make decisions, and then accept the consequences. If you’re not going to invite a friend to the coronation, he would feel snubbed, yet who knows what he could pull off during the ceremony?

Besides, both factions and individual characters take note of your actions. Decisions that you feel to be right could be harshly rebuked by others. Thus you have to keep in mind not only correctness and expedience of your actions, but also how they’re going to be seen by your vassals, trade partners, nobles and the people. Maybe you’re sure that the arrested peasant is innocent, but is he worthy of squabbling with Inquisition? And which of the vassals should you support - one who’s in the right by law, or one who can offer you a better deal?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36617318/4b9bd6ab3c5ed34a5f8b8641ce53d5213e7aabc3.jpg[/img]

[h3]Governance[/h3]
The whole march is under your purview, and it’s up to you what it will become in the future. A small part of these lands - your [b]Domain [/b]- is under your direct control. Indeed it lost luster during last decades, but should enough effort be applied, Demesne’s capital could find a worthy competitor in these lands.

Your influence is not constrained by your Domain, though; as a margrave, you can issue [b]edicts [/b]to be followed by everyone in the march. Through these edicts reform could be carried out - or your rule, strengthened. According to traditions, though, edicts have to be ratified by factions… Not a problem if you’re strong enough - then nobody would dare cross you, even if their opinions are different.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36617318/6889aa60688f82bc82b02777e7c48a7534e5d21d.png[/img]

The ways in which you solve disputes and deal with factions influence developments of the march, expressed in parameters such as [b]significance in trade, power of religion, popularity of local traditions[/b] and others (we will cover them in more details in later posts). Ports will accumulate wealth and the march will become a trade hub hosting traders from all over Demesne, if you  support trade guilds; On the other hand, it would empower these same guilds and traders controlling them, to the point of threatening traditional nobility or even your own rule.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36617318/9801dabd063b3ef54eb2d0dc9593a43fd98fcbe6.jpg[/img]

[h3]Story[/h3]
Protagonist’s father has disappeared, having launched a mysterious expedition. It certainly was important to him if he left ancestral lands before his son could return. Or, maybe, it’s a result of conspiracy? Either way, his disappearance should be investigated - even if just for you to avoid the same fate.

You will have to investigate particulars of that disappearance, and to get information from people of interests themselves - or from spies assigned to them. Not everyone is going to help voluntarily - many of them have their own secrets: Someone supports heretics, another runs from their past… Through learning these secrets you could get a lot of power - and dangerous enemies.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36617318/214c606c111569994b83ee19811b65b888ebce92.jpg[/img]

Maybe current events are connected to countless rumours that another Dark Decade is awaiting Demesne: There are talks that in the east for every suppressed rebellion two more take its place, entire towns disappear without trace in sandstorms of the south, and that even capital is no longer safe. You should pay attention to talks of your own march, though - barbarian tribes to the north, long thought toothless, are uniting under the banners of unknown leader…

Storyline is divided into several acts. In each of them you will have to make decisions that would influence its resolution and conditions in which the next is going to start. We’re striving to create a non-linear plot, thus many choices would significantly alter it as opposed to altering small details of the story.

We’ve tried to describe basics of the game in this post, and we’ll cover them in more detail in later posts. Stay tuned!
